intro.paragraph1: SoAI (Smart Orchestrator for Artificial Intelligence) manages local inference engines and remote AI providers from one WebUI. It presents their models through OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible APIs
intro.paragraph2: SoAI runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows. It is source-available and free for personal and homelab use. SoAI does not collect your data or send analytics, telemetry, or usage reports

gettingStarted.heading: Run your first model
gettingStarted.intro: SoAI can run models on this machine or connect to a remote provider. For a local model, follow steps 1 and 2. For a remote model, start at step 3. Both paths continue in Chat
gettingStarted.localBackend: For local inference, open Plugins and choose an engine. Select Install backend, choose a build for your operating system and hardware, then install it. Some backends need supported GPU drivers or other system components
gettingStarted.localModel: Open Models and select Add model once the backend is ready. You can search for a model to download or add model files already stored on the machine. Before the download starts, SoAI shows its size and estimates how much memory the model needs
gettingStarted.remoteModel: For remote inference, you can skip backend installation. Open Models, select Add model and then Add provider. Choose External, enter the provider name, API URL, API key, and an optional model filter
gettingStarted.chat: Open Chat after the model appears in the catalog. Select the model and send a message. SoAI starts its backend when needed, while the conversation settings control generation parameters and tool access
gettingStarted.api: Other applications can use the same model catalog through SoAI's OpenAI-compatible API. Set the application's OpenAI base URL to this SoAI instance and choose a model ID from /v1/models. If an administrator enabled API keys, add a bearer token
gettingStarted.troubleshooting: If a local model does not start, check its backend state on Plugins first. Plugins shows hardware compatibility and installation requirements. Open Logs for diagnostic details

models.heading: Use one model catalog and one API
models.catalog: A plugin connects SoAI to an inference engine or remote provider. The Plugins page installs and configures those connections, while Models shows the models they provide and stores the settings for each one. Applications connect through /v1/chat/completions, /v1/responses, and /v1/models, so switching engines or providers does not require a new client endpoint. Models remain in the catalog while their backend is stopped. Sending a request starts the required backend. If you set a limit on running backends, SoAI can stop an idle one to make room
models.virtualModels: A virtual model places several models behind one name. Use one to balance requests between backends or send work to another model when the first one is unavailable
models.plugins: All built-in plugins are MIT licensed, and anyone can build a new plugin with the SoAI plugin SDK. If an inference backend already provides an OpenAI-compatible API, connect it through the External plugin instead of writing a new one
models.engineGguf: Ollama and llama.cpp for GGUF models
models.engineVllm: vLLM for AWQ, GPTQ, and transformer models
models.engineCtranslate2: CTranslate2 for translation over the completion API
models.engineExternal: External for OpenAI-compatible providers such as OpenRouter, Groq, Together AI, and OpenAI

chatTools.heading: Work with models, tools, and files
chatTools.conversations: The Chat page keeps messages, model choice, generation parameters, and tool access together. You can change models between turns, compare responses, save the setup as a preset, or organize conversations into folders. Attach a file when the model needs the full item for the current message. Attach a knowledge source when you want SoAI to search indexed material and return the relevant passages. Add files, folders, and SoAI links from the composer
chatTools.tools: Chat mode is for conversation. Plan mode lets the model inspect a task and prepare steps. It blocks tools marked as destructive or missing valid destructive metadata, but other selected tools can still affect external systems. Execute mode lets it act with the tools you enabled. Tool calls and their results stay visible in the transcript, and protected actions can require your approval. Available tools can search the web, control a browser, work with files and terminals, query knowledge, process media, and connect to mail or calendars. Administrators decide which integrations and credentials are available. Agents can also ask questions, keep a plan, and split work into background subtasks. The Automation page runs one or more turns on a schedule and keeps each run as a conversation
chatTools.mcp: SoAI can expose its tools to authenticated MCP clients and connect to remote MCP servers. Remote tools appear beside the built-in tools after an administrator configures the server
chatTools.voice: Speech-to-text models can transcribe recordings or microphone input. Text-to-speech models can read answers aloud, while voice call mode supports a spoken conversation

filesKnowledge.heading: Manage files, knowledge, and saved prompts
filesKnowledge.files: The Files page is SoAI's file manager. Each account has its own folder, and an administrator can point several accounts at the same folder when they need a shared workspace. Search or navigate by path, upload files or whole folders, and switch between icon and list views. You can create and edit text files in the browser. Images, audio, video, and other documents open in the preview. You can rename, move, copy, download, or delete files and folders. To bring one into Chat, select Attach from Files or copy a file's SoAI link from its preview. SoAI reads the stored item without uploading a second copy. A direct attachment belongs to the current message, so use it when the model needs a specific file or folder for that request
filesKnowledge.knowledge: Use Knowledge when a conversation needs to consult a collection across later requests. You can index files and whole folders from your device, or load a folder stored in Files. Follow parsing, chunking, and embedding in the source status; search results include the source after processing finishes. An agent with the Knowledge tools enabled can fetch a web page into the conversation's index. Choose semantic similarity, MMR to reduce near-duplicate results, or Hybrid to combine semantic and keyword matching. Use the Knowledge settings to choose the embedding model, chunking method, chunk size and overlap, similarity threshold, and the number of passages sent to the model. If you change the embedding model or chunking settings, use Reindex to rebuild the collection
filesKnowledge.prompts: The Prompts page keeps instructions you expect to reuse. Name them, assign colors, search their names or contents, and duplicate or download several at once. Open the saved prompts picker in the chat composer to insert one. Choose a model to rewrite a saved prompt, compare the streamed result with the original, and save the revision as a new prompt

administration.heading: Check system health and maintain the host
administration.status: The Dashboard shows current system status and active work. Use Hardware for CPU, memory, disk, network, and GPU readings; Metrics for request history and token use; and Logs when you need diagnostic detail. Supported GPUs expose tuning controls for power, clocks, and fans. These changes affect the host, so use a tested profile and watch temperatures and stability
administration.operations: Terminal provides interactive shell sessions. Power can restart or stop SoAI and can control the host operating system. Access to both pages depends on account permissions
administration.maintenance: Backups live in Settings, while application updates use the Updates page. Verify a backup before relying on it, export copies you need off the host, and review the scope before a restore or reset. SoAI monitors backend health and stops sending requests to a plugin that keeps failing. The Plugins page shows recovery and quarantine states. Downloads, uploads, backups, and other large writes check reserved disk space before they begin

access.heading: Control who can connect and what they can do
access.access: A fresh install exposes only the setup wizard until the first user account exists. After setup, /v1/* accepts requests without authentication while no API keys exist. While any key exists, requests need a valid API key. OpenAI-compatible routes accept it as a bearer token; Anthropic-compatible routes also accept x-api-key. The MCP server requires a personal access token
access.users: Administrators assign role permissions for files, plugins, GPU controls, backups, Terminal, Power, and other protected areas. Permission changes apply to active sessions. Administrators with user-management access can review and revoke their own active sessions
access.network: Use HTTPS when other devices connect to SoAI. Keep the instance on a trusted local network or behind a VPN. Exposing SoAI to the open internet is discouraged. If you still plan to do so, review the security audit and configure the host for public access first. Offline mode blocks connections to public addresses. Local models, installed backends, the WebUI, and permitted private-network providers and MCP servers keep working. Public providers, downloads, update checks, and public web tools stop. Mail and calendar network operations stop even on private networks
access.plugins: A .soaiplugin file contains executable code. Install plugins only when you trust its source and publisher
